findings.passage: I am opposed to voter ID requirements for the same reasons — it creates barriers to voting with no evidence that it solves any real problem.
findings.note: Her written answer in the WESA candidate survey, in reply to a question on no-excuse mail-in voting and other voting-law changes. Date taken from the page URL.

findings.passage: Yes. I support no-excuse mail-in voting because voting needs to keep up with technology and we have the technology to ensure safe, secure, and accurate voting by mail.
findings.note: Same survey answer: supports no-excuse mail voting, drop boxes, early in-person voting, and automatic and same-day registration.

findings.passage: The issue is not and has never been voter fraud — it is voter disenfranchisement.
findings.note: Her answer in the WESA 2024 voter guide to a question that listed mail-in balloting, drop boxes and voter verification requirements; she also names automatic registration, early voting, mail-in pre-canvassing and county funding. Date is the page's publish date.
